rationales: The stop value -1 is excluded, but 0 comes before it when counting down, so 0 is included.
A negative step counts down, so the range is not empty when the start is above the stop.

quiz.q: When does the else clause of a for or while loop run?
options: Never; else belongs only to if
When the loop finishes without executing break
Only when the loop ran zero times
rationales: A loop can have an else clause.
It runs after a full loop too; running zero times is just one way of finishing without a break.

quiz.q: What is the value of i after for i in range(3): pass?
rationales: Names in the target list are not deleted when the loop ends.
range(3) stops before 3, so the last value assigned is 2.

options: Raises ValueError, because the lengths differ
rationales: That is what zip does by default, stopping at the shortest; strict=True changes it.
zip never pads with None; itertools.zip_longest does.

quiz.q: Which import style does PEP 8 advise against?
options: import os on one line and import sys on the next
rationales: That is the style PEP 8 recommends: imports on separate lines.
A plain import is fine; it keeps every name under its module's name.

quiz.q: You need each item of a list together with its position. Which loop is the best fit?
rationales: It works, but enumerate gives position and item directly, as the tutorial advises.
It needs a counter you must remember to update, an easy way to write an endless loop.

quiz.q: A program calls sys.exit() inside a try block that has a finally clause. What happens?
options: The program exits at once and the finally clause is skipped
The finally clause still runs, and then the program exits
sys.exit() only works outside try blocks
rationales: sys.exit() raises SystemExit, and finally clauses are honored as the exception passes.
sys.exit() only raises an exception; it can be called anywhere.
